title: One-sample t test
biology: Cell biologists measure oxygen consumption in independently cultured cell lines.
design: One measurement from each of 24 independent cultures; compare with a prespecified reference of 10 nmol/min.
other_examples: Offspring size versus a historical mean
question: Is mean oxygen consumption different from 10 nmol/min?
assumptions: No extreme outliers; normality matters more at small n
parametric: Investigate unusual values; retain genuine biology
Model log values only if a ratio/geometric mean answers the question
nonparametric: Sign test targets the median, not the mean
A bootstrap mean interval retains the mean target

plot_args.note: Put the measured response on the x-axis

practice: If the reference were 11 rather than 10, what would change in the hypothesis and R call?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1101)
d <- data.frame(culture = 1:24,
                oxygen = rnorm(24, mean = 10.8, sd = 1.5))
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
beeswarm(d$oxygen, horizontal = TRUE, method = "swarm",
         pch = 21, bg = "#246A73", col = "white", cex = 1.6,
         xlab = "Oxygen consumption (nmol/min)", ylab = "", yaxt = "n")
abline(v = 10, lty = 2, col = "#B7663E", lwd = 2)
legend("topleft", "Reference mean = 10", lty = 2,
       col = "#B7663E", bty = "n")
generating_model: 24 independent oxygen-consumption values are drawn from Normal(mean 10.8, SD 1.5). Each row is one culture.
generating_truth: The population mean is 10.8 nmol/min, so the reference-mean null of 10 is false; the true mean difference is +0.8.
teaching_point: The reference must express the biological question; the test is about a population mean.
